claudecfgManagedOnClaudeAi: Managed on claude.ai; view only here.
claudecfgZipTooLarge: The file is over 45 MB, which is too large for a Skill package
claudecfgConfigFooter: These change this device's own Claude Code configuration (~/.claude), which also applies to claude in a terminal there.
claudecfgDefaultsFooter: Used for new conversations on this device. Stored in this device's own Claude Code settings, the same ones /model and /effort save as defaults in a terminal there; choices made in a conversation apply only to it. Thinking effort is stored per model. The context window is the most tokens a session uses; auto-compact goes by it, or by the model's own window if that is smaller.
claudecfgNotRead: Claude Code settings not loaded yet
claudecfgEffortFooter: New conversations on this device use the setting for their model, the same one /effort saves as default in a terminal there. Models without their own setting use “Other models”.
claudecfgClaudeFooter: Applies only to conversations Zeta starts on this device. The idle timeout takes effect at once; the rest when a process next starts.
claudecfgAutoTitleSummary: Claude Code writes a short title after the first reply; renamed conversations are left alone
claudecfgAgentNameInvalid: Use only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit
claudecfgAgentWhenMissing: Describe when to use it before saving
claudecfgAgentsFooter: Stored in ~/.claude/agents and available in every project. Claude picks one by its “When to use”, or you can name one in a conversation.
claudecfgAgentsEmptyHint: Ask Claude to write one, or click “New” at the top right
claudecfgAgentNameFooter: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, such as code-reviewer.
claudecfgAgentWhenFooter: Claude decides from this whether to hand a task to it, so say clearly what it's good at.
claudecfgAgentWhenPlaceholder: e.g. Review changes after code edits, finding bugs and unclear spots
claudecfgAgentPromptFooter: Describe its role and how it works. It can't see the main conversation, only this prompt and the task it's given.
claudecfgAgentExtraKeys: Also sets {keys}, which are kept as they are when saving.
claudecfgAgentModelFooter: By default it uses the main conversation's model.
claudecfgAgentToolsFooter: With “All tools” off, it can use only the checked ones. Write MCP tools as mcp__server__tool, separated by commas.
claudecfgMemoryInstructionsFooter: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md holds your standing instructions for Claude, shared by all projects. Changes apply to conversations started afterwards.
claudecfgMemoryInstructionsMissing: Not created yet; open it to start writing
claudecfgMemoryInstructionsPlaceholder: e.g. Answer in English; my main stack is Go; explain your plan before changing code
claudecfgAutoMemoryFooter: Claude notes your preferences, corrections and project background during conversations. The switch applies to all projects; when it's off, memories are kept but no longer read or written.
claudecfgAutoMemoryForcedOff: Turned off by an environment variable; can't be changed here
claudecfgMemoryIndexPlaceholder: One memory per line: - [Title](file.md) — one-line summary
claudecfgMemoryFilesEmpty: No memories for this project yet
claudecfgMemoryFilesEmptyHint: What Claude remembers shows up here
claudecfgDocumentTooLarge: Over the 1 MiB limit; please shorten it
claudecfgConflictMessage: This file changed while you were editing it, most likely because Claude updated it in a conversation. Saving overwrites it with your version.
claudecfgMemoryDeleteMessage: Deletes {file} and removes its line from MEMORY.md. This can't be undone.
claudecfgMcpShadowedBy: Overridden by a server of the same name in “{scope}”
claudecfgMcpFooter: New servers are available in every project. Changes apply to conversations started afterwards.
claudecfgMcpEmptyHint: Click “Add server” at the top right
claudecfgMcpNameInvalid: Use only letters, digits, underscores and hyphens in the name
claudecfgMcpURLInvalid: The URL must start with http:// or https://
claudecfgMcpEnvInvalid: Put one environment variable per line, as KEY=VALUE
claudecfgMcpEnvPlaceholder: Environment variables (optional, one KEY=VALUE per line)
claudecfgMcpDeleteSummary: Its URL, token and settings will be removed from the configuration
claudecfgMcpAuthOAuth: OAuth: sign in with /mcp in claude in a terminal
claudecfgToolsConnectHint: Connect to the server to list its tools
claudecfgToolsOAuth: Not available for servers that sign in with OAuth
claudecfgMcpTokenHint: Enter a new token, or leave it empty to remove authentication. The current token isn't shown.
claudecfgMcpDeleteMessage: Delete {name}? Its URL, token and settings will be removed from the configuration. This can't be undone.
claudecfgPermSpecific: {count, plural, one {Plus # rule with arguments} other {Plus # rules with arguments}}
claudecfgPermissionsIntro: The strictest rule wins, in the order Deny > Ask > Allow, however specific a rule is. Ask and Deny still apply in bypass permissions mode. Changes apply to all projects and to conversations started afterwards.
claudecfgPermBulkAdd: {count, plural, one {Add to {behavior} (# rule): {rules}} other {Add to {behavior} (# rules): {rules}}}
claudecfgPermBulkRemove: {count, plural, one {Remove from {behavior} (# rule): {rules}} other {Remove from {behavior} (# rules): {rules}}}
claudecfgPermNoToolsWarning: Once they're off, Claude can't even read or write files or run commands; it can only chat and use MCP tools.
claudecfgPermRulesFooter: Rules with arguments are changed only here; the menus above leave them alone.
claudecfgPermRulesEmptyHint: Click “Add rule” at the top right
claudecfgPermRuleMalformed: {behavior} · Unbalanced parentheses, so Claude Code can't read this rule
claudecfgPermRuleHelp: Write Tool or Tool(arguments), such as Bash(npm run test:*), Read(./.env), Edit(src/**), WebFetch(domain:github.com) or mcp__github (the whole server).
claudecfgPermServerFooter: The whole-server setting covers each of its tools; where a tool has its own setting too, the stricter one wins.
claudecfgPermServerOAuth: To set tools one by one, write {rule}__tool under “Rules” on the previous page.
claudecfgSkillInstalledMessage: “{name}” is installed. Claude will use it when needed.
claudecfgSkillInstalledDisabled: “{name}” is installed but set to disabled. Turn it on to use it.
claudecfgSkillPick: Choose a Skill package that contains SKILL.md
claudecfgSkillsUserFooter: Installed in ~/.claude/skills. Turning one off keeps its files, but Claude stops using it. Changes apply to conversations started afterwards.
claudecfgSkillsEmptyHint: Import a ZIP, or ask Claude to write one
claudecfgSkillMissingFileDetail: This folder has no SKILL.md, so Claude Code won't treat it as a Skill.
claudecfgSkillReplaceMessage: A Skill named “{name}” already exists. Replacing it overwrites all of its current files.
claudecfgSkillDeleteMessage: Deletes the whole “{name}” folder. You'll have to import it again to get it back.
claudecfgModelsPending: Asking Claude Code on this device for its model list; showing the common ones for now.
claudecfgDocumentEmptyEdit: Nothing here yet. Click to edit
aboutCreditEta: The reference for Zeta, whose features and interactions follow it (GPL-3.0)
aboutCreditClaudeCode: Anthropic's coding agent; Zeta is a client for it
aboutCreditMygo: The desktop UI framework: windows, controls, layout and drawing (MIT)
aboutCreditCrypto: SSH for direct connections to devices (BSD-3-Clause)
aboutCreditImage: Scaling attached images and decoding WebP and BMP (BSD-3-Clause)
aboutCreditCoui: Some icons come from its icon set, coui-icons (Apache-2.0)
aboutCreditRatex: Typesets math in replies, as in the phone app (MIT)
